title: Grey's Anatomy
wiki_lead:
Grey's Anatomy is an American medical drama television series focusing on the personal and professional lives of surgical interns, residents, and attendings at the fictional Seattle Grace Hospital (later renamed Seattle Grace Mercy West Hospital, and currently Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital). The series premiered on March 27, 2005, on ABC as a mid-season replacement and has been renewed annually for two decades. Its title is a mixture of the protagonist's surname and the name of the classic human anatomy textbook Gray's Anatomy. Writer Shonda Rhimes developed the pilot and served as showrunner, head writer, and executive producer until stepping down in 2015. Set in Seattle, Washington, the series is filmed primarily in Los Angeles, California.
The original cast consisted of nine star-billed actors: Ellen Pompeo, Sandra Oh, Katherine Heigl, Justin Chambers, T. R. Knight, Chandra Wilson, James Pickens Jr., Isaiah Washington, and Patrick Dempsey. For most of its run, the series revolves around Dr. Meredith Grey (Pompeo), chronicling her progression from surgical intern to fully-qualified doctor. The cast has undergone major changes throughout the series' run, with only three original members remaining by the 19th season – Pompeo, Wilson, and Pickens. Pompeo stepped back from the series in its 19th season, at which point the show shifted to more of an ensemble format. In March 2026, ABC renewed the series for a 23rd season, which is set to premiere in the fall of 2026. Grey's Anatomy has two spin-off series: Private Practice (2007–2013) and Station 19 (2018–2024); as well as a web series, Grey's Anatomy: B-Team.
Grey's Anatomy is the longest-running scripted primetime show currently airing on ABC, and the longest scripted primetime series carried by ABC. The series brought many series regulars, including Pompeo, Oh, and Dempsey, to worldwide recognition; they were among the five highest-earning television actors in 2013. Once among the overall top 10 shows in the United States, the show's ratings have fallen, although as of 2017 it was still one of the highest-rated shows among the 18–49 demographic. As of February 2023, Grey's Anatomy was ranked the 10th most popular on-demand program.
Grey's Anatomy has been well received by critics throughout much of its run and has been included in various critics' year-end top 10 lists. Cosmopolitan and Entertainment Weekly have listed it as one of the greatest television series of all time. Since its inception, the show has been described by the media outlets as a television "phenomenon" or a "juggernaut", owing to its longevity and dominant ratings. It is considered to have had a significant effect on popular culture and has received numerous awards, including the Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Drama and a total of 38 Primetime Emmy Award nominations, including 2 for Outstanding Drama Series. The cast members have also received accolades for their individual performances.

grok_lead: Grey's Anatomy is an American medical drama television series created by Shonda Rhimes that premiered on the American Broadcasting Company (ABC) on March 27, 2005. The series centers on the personal and professional lives of surgeons at the fictional Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital (formerly Seattle Grace Hospital) in Seattle, Washington, as they navigate complex medical cases, ethical dilemmas, and interpersonal relationships. As of November 2025, Grey's Anatomy is in its 22nd season, with over 450 episodes aired, establishing it as the longest-running scripted primetime medical drama in U.S. television history. The show stars Ellen Pompeo as Meredith Grey, a talented but emotionally complex surgeon whose journey from intern to chief of surgery anchors the narrative, alongside a rotating ensemble including Chandra Wilson as the steadfast Miranda Bailey, James Pickens Jr. as the veteran Richard Webber, and Kevin McKidd as the resilient Owen Hunt. Created under Shondaland Productions, Grey's Anatomy is renowned for its fast-paced storytelling, blending high-stakes surgeries with themes of romance, loss, and resilience, often drawing from real medical procedures while emphasizing diverse representation among its characters. Grey's Anatomy has garnered significant acclaim, winning the Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series â Drama in 2007 and receiving 39 Primetime Emmy Award nominations, including the Outstanding Supporting Actress win for Katherine Heigl in 2007 and the Outstanding Guest Actress win for Loretta Devine in 2011. The series has also spawned two spin-offs: Private Practice (2007â2013), which followed Dr. Addison Montgomery's relocation to Los Angeles, and Station 19 (2018â2024), a firefighter drama intersecting with the hospital's world through shared characters and crossovers. Its enduring popularity has made it a cultural phenomenon, influencing medical dramas and contributing to ABC's Thursday night lineup for two decades.
